title: 三个小烤盘  (Three Small Baking Tins)

segments.t: In the café corner, Mei hands out clean white aprons to Peng and Qing. They are about to bake three small test cakes with three different glazes to solve the smudged recipe line. Listen in first.
志鹏、小晴，快把这两条白围裙穿上！
大厨，我已经把三个圆烤盘放在铁炉架上啦。
卡片最后一行字晕开了，只剩左边一个虫字旁……
所以我们要烤三个小莓果杏仁蛋糕，试三种甜糖霜！
第一盘用柠檬汁加糖——老陈喜欢吃酸的。
第二盘撒厚厚的粗糖，烤出脆壳，志豪肯定爱吃。
第三盘的味道最神秘——温的虫字旁到底是什么呢？
会不会是蚂蚁？温蚂蚁蛋糕听起来太吓人了吧！
志鹏真会开玩笑，哪有菜谱教人烤蚂蚁吃的？
不管怎样，我们先把莓果和杏仁拌进面糊里！
面糊香得连窗外的小鸟都飞过来看热闹啦。
那就请大厨关上烤箱门，让蛋糕慢慢变大吧！
Now let's go through it line by line with the English translation.
志鹏、小晴，快把这两条白围裙穿上！
'Peng, Qing, hurry and put on these two white aprons!' "Tiao" is the counter for long things like aprons or ribbons, and "chuan shang" pairs "wear" with the direction "up / onto".
大厨，我已经把三个圆烤盘放在铁炉架上啦。
'Chef, I have already placed the three round baking tins on the iron stove rack.' Mandarin builds "kaopan" from "bake" and "plate", and "yijing" states that Peng "already" set them out.
卡片最后一行字晕开了，只剩左边一个虫字旁……

'The last line of the card is smudged, leaving only an insect character-side on the left...' "Zuihou" means "most back" or "final", and "chong zi pang" refers to the "insect component" used in words like bee or honey.
所以我们要烤三个小莓果杏仁蛋糕，试三种甜糖霜！

'So we must bake three small berry-and-almond cakes and test three sweet glazes!' Counting "zhong" means "kinds / varieties" of glaze, and "tangshuang" combines "sugar" and "frost" for frosting or glaze.
第一盘用柠檬汁加糖——老陈喜欢吃酸的。
'Tin One uses lemon juice and sugar—Chen likes eating sour things.' "Diyi" turns "one" into "first", and "zhi" gives the liquid "juice" squeezed from the lemon.
第二盘撒厚厚的粗糖，烤出脆壳，志豪肯定爱吃。

'Tin Two gets a thick sprinkle of coarse sugar baked into a crisp crust, which Hao will definitely love eating.' Repeating "hou" ("thick") as "houhou" emphasizes the heavy layer, and "cu tang" names "coarse" large-crystal sugar.
第三盘的味道最神秘——温的虫字旁到底是什么呢？

'The flavour of Tin Three is the most mysterious—what on earth is the warm insect-side character?' Adding "zui" ("most") before "shenmi" ("mysterious") builds the superlative, while "daodi" presses "what on earth?"
会不会是蚂蚁？温蚂蚁蛋糕听起来太吓人了吧！
'Could it be ants? Warm ant cake sounds too terrifying, right!' "Hui bu hui" asks "could it or could it not be", and "ting qilai" means "sounds like" to Peng's ears.
志鹏真会开玩笑，哪有菜谱教人烤蚂蚁吃的？
'Peng is really good at joking; what recipe teaches people to bake and eat ants?' "Zhen hui" says he "truly knows how" to joke, and "na you" sceptically asks "where is there" such a recipe.
不管怎样，我们先把莓果和杏仁拌进面糊里！
'Regardless, let us first stir the berries and almonds into the batter!' Opening with "buguan zenyang" brushes aside the ant joke with "no matter what", and "ban jin" means "stir into".
面糊香得连窗外的小鸟都飞过来看热闹啦。

'The batter smells so fragrant that even the little birds outside the window are flying over to watch the fun.' "Lian... dou..." wraps around the birds to mean "even they all...", and "kan renao" means looking at a lively scene.
那就请大厨关上烤箱门，让蛋糕慢慢变大吧！
'Then Chef please close the oven door and let the cakes slowly grow big!' Doubling "man" ("slow") gently stretches out "manman", while "bian da" tracks the cakes "becoming big" as they rise.
Now let's listen to the whole conversation one last time.

Mei shuts the heavy oven door as Peng and Qing watch through the glass. The bake-off has begun! See you next time.
下次见！
